title: 1st Abyss 1st Matter In Universal Questions Denial Is Worthless Against Proof

questions.question: Why does the passage say it will speak only about two dangers to strong faith in this time?
questions.answer: Because the truth has already been clearly proved elsewhere, so this part only points out two big causes of doubt.

questions.question: What image is used for these dangers to faith?
questions.answer: They are described as two deep pits or abysses.

questions.question: How many matters are given as a way to be saved from the first abyss?
questions.answer: Two matters are given.

questions.question: In the first matter, what is said about denial when clear proof is present?
questions.answer: It is weak and has little value.

questions.question: What example is used to show this point about proof and denial?
questions.answer: The example of seeing the new moon at the start of Ramadan.

questions.question: In that example, whose statement carries weight: the few who saw it or the many who did not?
questions.answer: The few who saw it carry weight because they have proof.

questions.question: Why do people who confirm something strengthen one another?
questions.answer: Because they are pointing to the same real thing, so their witness joins together.

questions.question: Why do people who deny something not truly support one another in the same way?
questions.answer: Because each one is only speaking from his own limited view and stays separate from the others.

questions.question: If one person says something exists and another says it does not, which side is easier to prove according to the passage?
questions.answer: The side that says it exists is easier to prove.

questions.question: Why is denying the existence of something everywhere much harder?
questions.answer: Because the person would have to search all places and even all times to prove it is nowhere.

questions.question: What mistake do deniers make when judging big matters?
questions.answer: They judge by their own selves, minds, and eyesight instead of the reality itself.

questions.question: According to the passage, what can a person honestly say if he has not seen something?
questions.answer: He can say that he did not see it and so he does not believe it.

questions.question: What can he not truthfully say about reality itself?
questions.answer: He cannot truthfully say that it does not exist at all.

questions.question: What does the passage choose to explain instead of repeating all the proof for the truth?
questions.answer: It explains two major causes that disturb certainty of faith in this age.

questions.question: How is the first danger introduced?
questions.answer: It is introduced as an abyss from which people need saving.

questions.question: What is the first lesson in escaping that danger?
questions.answer: The first lesson is that denial is powerless against solid proof.

questions.question: Which religious event is used as an example of this lesson?
questions.answer: The sighting of the Ramadan crescent.

questions.question: If two ordinary people truly see the crescent, what happens to the denial of many important people who did not see it?
questions.answer: Their denial loses force because not seeing it is not proof against those who did.

questions.question: Why does confirmation lead to agreement?
questions.answer: Because each confirming person adds support to the same truth.

questions.question: Why does denial not produce the same kind of agreement?
questions.answer: Because each denial stands by itself and comes from personal limits.

questions.question: What picture is given of two people who affirm something real?
questions.answer: One points it out, and the other joins him by seeing the same thing.

questions.question: What basic rule is stated about a broad denial that is not tied to one exact place?
questions.answer: It cannot be properly proved.

questions.question: Why can the existence of one thing be shown with only one sign?
questions.answer: Because one clear indication can show that it is there.

questions.question: Why would proving non-existence everywhere be extremely hard?
questions.answer: Because it would require a complete search through the whole world and all times.

questions.question: What is wrong with judging by only one’s own sight and mind?
questions.answer: It limits truth to personal experience instead of reality itself.

questions.question: What is the difference between saying “I do not see it” and saying “It is not real”?
questions.answer: The first is about personal experience, but the second makes a huge claim about all reality.

questions.question: Why does the passage call such a huge claim false in belief matters?
questions.answer: Because belief matters concern the whole universe, and no denier has that full knowledge.

questions.question: What does the passage say has already been established with strong evidence?
questions.answer: The main truth about faith has already been firmly shown.

questions.question: Why are only four-question-style limits and two abysses mentioned here?
questions.answer: Because this section is narrowing the focus to major doubts rather than repeating every proof.

questions.question: What is the goal of the two matters under the first abyss?
questions.answer: They are meant to rescue a person from that danger.

questions.question: In the first matter, what happens when proof and denial face each other?
questions.answer: Proof stands firm, while denial remains weak.

questions.question: Why is the new moon example a good fit for this point?
questions.answer: Because seeing the moon is direct evidence, while not seeing it is only lack of sight.

questions.question: What does the example show about the number of people on each side?
questions.answer: A larger number on the denying side does not defeat true witness on the affirming side.

questions.question: How do people who confirm a real thing become stronger together?
questions.answer: They all refer to the same reality, so their statements join and support each other.

questions.question: Why does each denier remain on his own?
questions.answer: Because his denial comes from his own limits, not from a shared direct proof.

questions.question: What makes proving existence easier than proving total non-existence?
questions.answer: Existence can be shown by one clear sign, but non-existence needs complete checking everywhere.

questions.question: What huge task would someone have to do to prove something never existed?
questions.answer: He would have to inspect the whole world and all earlier times.

questions.question: What does the passage say deniers are really judging by?
questions.answer: Their own inner state, understanding, and vision.

questions.question: What is a truthful personal statement a denier may make?
questions.answer: He may say that he himself does not see or know it.

questions.question: What makes a denial of reality itself so dangerous?
questions.answer: It goes beyond personal ignorance and pretends to know all reality.

questions.question: In the short summary, how is affirmation described?
questions.answer: As one united result in which each instance helps the others.

questions.question: In the short summary, how is negation described?
questions.answer: As many separate results because each person speaks from his own viewpoint.

questions.question: What does this passage focus on instead of giving the full proof again?
questions.answer: It focuses on two major causes of doubt that shake faith today.

questions.question: What word in the passage helps us imagine these dangers as very serious?
questions.answer: The word “abyss” shows they are very serious and dangerous.

questions.question: How does the passage begin helping people escape the first abyss?
questions.answer: It gives two matters, starting with a lesson about proof and denial.

questions.question: What is the central teaching of the first matter?
questions.answer: Denial cannot stand strong against real proof.

questions.question: Which month’s moon is used as an example?
questions.answer: Ramadan’s beginning moon.

questions.question: What is more valuable in that example: seeing or not seeing?
questions.answer: Seeing is more valuable because it gives evidence.

questions.question: Why does “I did not see it” fail to defeat “I saw it”?
questions.answer: Because not seeing something is not the same as proving it is absent.

questions.question: What happens when several people affirm the same fact?
questions.answer: Their statements support one another and become stronger together.

questions.question: Why do several denials not become strong in the same way?
questions.answer: Because each denial is separate and based on that person’s own lack of sight or knowledge.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about proving that something exists?
questions.answer: One sign can be enough to show existence.

questions.question: What does it teach about proving that something does not exist anywhere?
questions.answer: That would require a complete search everywhere, which is far harder.

questions.question: What problem comes from judging with only one’s own mind and eyes?
questions.answer: A person mistakes his own limits for the limits of reality.

questions.question: Which statement stays within honesty: “I don’t see it” or “It is not real at all”?
questions.answer: “I don’t see it” stays within honesty.

questions.question: Why is the second statement too big for a person to make?
questions.answer: Because it claims complete knowledge that a person does not have.

questions.question: What brief conclusion is given about affirmation?
questions.answer: It is one and united, so each part helps the others.

questions.question: What brief conclusion is given about negation?
questions.answer: It is many and divided, so the parts do not truly help one another.

questions.question: Why does the passage not fully explain the truth again here?
questions.answer: Because it says that truth has already been proved strongly elsewhere.

questions.question: What does it choose to explain in this section?
questions.answer: It explains two deep causes of doubt that weaken certainty of faith.

questions.question: What are the first means of rescue from the first danger called?
questions.answer: They are called two matters.

questions.question: What does the first matter teach about saying “no” to a proven truth?
questions.answer: That such denial is very weak.

questions.question: What example from Islamic life is used to make this easy to understand?
questions.answer: The report of seeing the Ramadan crescent.

questions.question: If many people miss seeing the moon, why does that not cancel the witness of the few who saw it?
questions.answer: Because missing it is not proof that it was not there.

questions.question: What causes agreement when people affirm something?
questions.answer: They are all confirming the same reality.

questions.question: Why does denial stay scattered?
questions.answer: Because each person denies from his own separate limitation.

questions.question: What simple action in the example shows how affirmers help one another?
questions.answer: One points to the moon and another sees the same thing.

questions.question: What rule is given about a general denial with no exact target?
questions.answer: It cannot be established as proof.

questions.question: Why is one clue enough on the side of existence?
questions.answer: Because existence only needs one real sign to be shown.

questions.question: Why is denial of existence everywhere almost impossible to establish?
questions.answer: Because the whole world and even past times would have to be checked.

questions.question: What is the honest limit of a denier’s claim?
questions.answer: He can only speak about his own not seeing or not knowing.

questions.question: What happens if he goes beyond that and denies actual reality?
questions.answer: He makes a false claim far bigger than his knowledge.

questions.question: What is the main difference between affirmation and negation in the short summary?
questions.answer: Affirmation joins into one strong whole, while negation breaks into many isolated parts.

questions.question: What lesson should believers learn from that difference?
questions.answer: They should not be troubled by the seeming majority of deniers.

questions.question: What has already been done with strong evidence before this section begins its special discussion?
questions.answer: The main truth has already been firmly demonstrated.

questions.question: What is this section trying to address for readers living in this age?
questions.answer: It is addressing two serious sources of hesitation in faith.

questions.question: For the first source of hesitation, how many helps are given?
questions.answer: Two helps are given.

questions.question: What does the first help say about denial compared with proof?
questions.answer: Denial is weak when proof is present.

questions.question: What example from the Islamic calendar is used to explain that idea?
questions.answer: The sighting of the new moon for Ramadan.

questions.question: What matters more in that example: direct witness or lack of witness?
questions.answer: Direct witness matters more.

questions.question: Why can affirming witnesses stand together?
questions.answer: Because they are testifying to the same thing that really exists.

questions.question: Why can denying voices not unite in the same strong way?
questions.answer: Because each one only speaks from his own separate inability to see.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says broad denial cannot be proved?
questions.answer: It means a person cannot prove something is nowhere if he has not checked every possible place.

questions.question: How can existence be shown in a much easier way?
questions.answer: It can be shown by one clear indication.

questions.question: What would be required to prove total non-existence?
questions.answer: A complete search through the whole world and across time.

questions.question: According to the passage, from where do deniers often make their judgments?
questions.answer: From their own souls, intelligence, and vision.

questions.question: What statement about personal experience is acceptable?
questions.answer: Saying that one does not see or know it.

questions.question: What statement about reality goes too far?
questions.answer: Saying that it does not exist in truth.

questions.question: Why is this extra serious in belief matters?
questions.answer: Because belief matters relate to the whole universe, not just one small area.

questions.question: What does the short summary teach about the structure of affirmation?
questions.answer: It is single in result, so affirmations support one another.

questions.question: What does it teach about the structure of negation?
questions.answer: It becomes multiple because each person adds his own separate viewpoint.

questions.question: What conclusion should a believer draw from this about the majority of deniers?
questions.answer: Their large numbers do not give them real proof or lasting strength.
